title: Horizon and Summit
premise: Jonah Vane, estranged daughter of a disgraced archaeologist, survives by salvaging what others overlook—until a dying prospector trades her a map to the Meridian's wreck in exchange for a promise: deliver the truth of what the salvage fleet buried there to his daughter. Pursued by the fleet's ruthless captain and haunted by the father she never forgave, Jonah races the tides to a wreck that holds both a fortune and proof of a massacre the fleet's owners committed decades ago. In the flooded hold, she finds her father's final expedition notes—he died uncovering the same truth—and must choose between selling the evidence for the fortune that would free her, or giving it away to keep her promise. She gives it away, sinking the salvage fleet's claim in court and finally surfacing from the invisibility she hid inside.
about_author: Ulyana Fairweather is a former maritime surveyor who spent six seasons charting wrecks off the northern coast before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people the sea keeps, and the debts they carry ashore.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In the port town of Greywater, Jonah salvages scrap and dodges the salvage fleet's enforcers, who are buying up every chart on the coast. She's established as sharp, solitary, and one bad week from ruin. Emotional beat: the exhausting cost of staying invisible.

chapters.title: A Map for a Promise
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A dying prospector, Elias Crane, finds her and trades a hand-drawn map to the Meridian's wreck for her sworn word: bring the truth to his daughter, Maren, in the city of Corvess. He dies before explaining what the truth is. Emotional beat: the trap of a promise given too easily.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She deciphers the map—six tides until the wreck's air pocket floods for the season—and realizes the fleet's captain, Ada Kessler, is hunting the same coordinates. She steals a skiff and slips out of Greywater. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold Charts
chapters.summary: Kessler's POV. Aboard the salvage flagship, Kessler interrogates a chart-seller and learns a Vane has the map. Her chapters reveal she isn't just chasing treasure; she's erasing what her employers buried on the Meridian. Emotional beat: cold competence hiding a rot of guilt.

chapters.title: Stormwater
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A storm wrecks her skiff on a shoal island where she's rescued—reluctantly—by Tull, a fleet deserter who recognizes the map and hates Kessler. He offers passage in exchange for a share. Emotional beat: the risk of trusting anyone.

chapters.title: What the Hold Keeps
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, with a memory interlude of her father. Diving the Meridian's outer hull, Jonah finds a sealed strongbox and, inside it, her father's expedition notes—he reached this wreck years ago and died for what he documented. Emotional beat: grief colliding with the inheritance she never wanted.

chapters.title: The Price of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Tull's POV. Tull discovers the strongbox's second compartment: a ledger naming the fleet's owners in the massacre of the Meridian's crew. He must decide whether to sell it to Kessler, who has offered amnesty to any deserter who betrays Jonah. Emotional beat: survival versus conscience.

chapters.title: Two Tides Down
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Kessler's ships close in; Tull's betrayal is revealed—but he turned Kessler down, and they flee together into the flooded inner hold as the tide turns. Cornered, Jonah reads her father's final page aloud: he chose the truth over the fortune, too. Emotional beat: the last tide, and the choice it forces.

chapters.title: The Drowning Room
chapters.summary: Alternating Jonah and Kessler POVs. In the air pocket, Kessler offers Jonah everything—the fortune, freedom, erasure—in exchange for the ledger. Jonah refuses, and as the room floods, Kessler, unable to shoot the one witness who understands her guilt, lets her go and drowns with the wreck's secret half-buried. Emotional beat: the climax—mercy as the sharpest justice.

chapters.title: Above Water
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Half-drowned, Jonah delivers the ledger to Maren in Corvess; the owners fall, the fleet is impounded, and the fortune dissolves into court costs. Jonah keeps only the compass and her father's notes, and for the first time signs her own name to a salvage claim. Emotional beat: visible at last, and unafraid of it.
